The register says applicant is "Avery Berkel" and the document says "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd".

Hmm. Are these the same company? Avery Berkel and Avery Weigh-Tronix — Avery Berkel is a brand/company that was part of Weigh-Tronix. Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd is the legal entity name, while Avery Berkel is the brand name. They're related companies — Avery Berkel was a weighing company in Birmingham, UK, which became part of Avery Weigh-Tronix (a division of ITW). Actually the legal entity that held OIML certificates in 2009... NWML certificates for R76/1992 around 2009 were often issued to "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" (legal name) whose brand is "Avery Berkel".

Is this "same-entity"? The rules: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity." "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

"Avery Berkel" vs "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" — these are not mere spelling drift; they're different name forms. But they refer to the same manufacturer historically. Avery Berkel Limited changed name to Avery Weigh-Tronix Limited? Actually, Avery Berkel (the UK weighing scale maker) was acquired and merged into Weigh-Tronix, becoming Avery Weigh-Tronix. The brand "Avery Berkel" continues. In 2009, the legal entity on the certificate is "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" while the register may have recorded brand "Avery Berkel".

Which verdict? The options: same-entity, different-entity, document-noise, unverifiable.

Is this verifiable that they're the same? From general knowledge, Avery Berkel is a trading name of Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd (part of ITW). The certificate is a legal instrument; the legal name is Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd. So best value = document's value if considered same-entity? The rules say same-entity gives... actually the rules don't explicitly say best value for same-entity for names; for number/year format differences, register canonical form. For applicant name conflicts, hmm.

The rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Given the certificate document says "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd", that's the legally responsible party. The register's "Avery Berkel" is a brand/short form. Are they "genuinely different"? They denote the same manufacturer — Avery Berkel is the brand of Avery Weigh-Tronix. So same-entity in substance.

Given the fused record should carry the legal instrument's value: "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd". Verdict: same-entity? The mapping between "Avery Berkel" and "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" is a brand vs legal name of the same company lineage. Since certificate is the legal instrument, best_value = document value.

But wait — should the verdict be "different-entity"? They are literally different names, and "Avery Berkel" and "Avery Weigh-Tronix" were historically separate companies merged (Weigh-Tronix acquired Avery Berkel in 2000ish; Avery Weigh-Tronix is the merged entity). By 2009, "Avery Berkel" existed only as a brand under Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd. So the legal entity is Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd; "Avery Berkel" is a trading name. The certificate holder is the same organization. I'd say same-entity (brand vs legal name), best_value = document's legal name.

Alternatively, could argue different-entity: best_value = document's, which yields the same best_value anyway. The difference is the verdict. The rules say same-entity covers "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences" — this is more than that; it's a brand vs corporate name. But "genuinely different company" — it's not a genuinely different company; it's the same manufacturer under brand vs legal name. I'll go with same-entity, best_value = "Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd" since the certificate is the legal instrument and the register likely normalized to brand.

One sentence why: Avery Berkel is the trading brand of Avery Weigh-Tronix Ltd, the same certificate holder; keep the certificate's legal name.
